problem_entry: Minimum-weight k-edge subtrees, from oil-field leasing and facility layout (abstract).
key_idea: Complexity frontier plus a separable IP formulation (abstract).
assumptions: Undirected graph with edge weights; subtrees with exactly k edges (abstract).
proof_devices: Strong NP-hardness proof and polynomial case on trees (abstract)
Exact separation routine for generalized subtour elimination constraints (abstract)
experiments: none mentioned in the abstract

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: Hardness in general, polynomial special cases alongside
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Strongly NP-hard in general, polynomial when G is a tree; also S039, S048 and H002 in batch a2-01.

coauthors: H. W. Hamacher, K. Jørnsten, F. Maffioli

quotes.text: Although the general problem is shown to be strongly NP hard, it can be solved in polynomial time if G is itself a tree.

key_idea: Not stated beyond the definition; by the title, odd cut-sets and odd cycles for separation (inferred from title).
assumptions: P = conv{x integer : Ax <= b, x >= 0}, A and b integer (abstract).
experiments: not stated in the abstract
coauthors: none on the record (the 1996 journal paper of the same title, H002, is with Caprara; works.json note)

title: The precedence-constrained asymmetric traveling salesman polytope
contribution: With Balas and Pulleyblank: valid inequality families for the precedence-constrained ATS polytope with polynomial separation for important subfamilies, its dimension, and facetness of the two main classes under stated assumptions.
problem_entry: Precedence constraints as the most frequent side constraints of TSP applications (abstract).
key_idea: Inequality families, polynomial separation, dimension and facetness for the PCATS polytope (abstract).
assumptions: Precedence-constrained directed graph; facetness under unspecified reasonable assumptions (abstract).
proof_devices: Polynomial-time separation algorithms for important subfamilies (abstract)
Dimension of the PCATS polytope (abstract)
Facet proofs for the two main classes (abstract)
experiments: none (polyhedral theory; abstract)
limits_future: Facetness holds under assumptions not given in the abstract (abstract).

quotes.text: They derive several families of valid inequalities, and give polynomial time separation algorithms for important subfamilies.

title: Clique tree inequalities define facets of the asymmetric traveling salesman polytope
contribution: Sole author: shows that the Grötschel-Pulleyblank clique tree inequalities define facets of the asymmetric traveling salesman polytope and its monotonization, through a recursive definition of clique trees by number of teeth.
problem_entry: An open facetness question carried over from the symmetric polytope (abstract).
key_idea: Recursive definition of clique trees by teeth, enabling induction (abstract).
assumptions: ATS polytope and its monotonization (abstract).
proof_devices: New recursive definition of clique tree, induction on the number of teeth rather than handles (abstract)
experiments: none (polyhedral theory; abstract)
positioning: Generalizes the corresponding result for symmetric polytopes (abstract).
transferable: If induction on the usual parameter of a structure stalls, redefine the structure recursively along another parameter (teeth instead of handles) and induct on that (abstract).

quotes.text: The proof makes use of a new recursive definition of clique tree, based on induction on the number of its ‘teeth’ rather than of its ‘handles’.

title: Odd Cut-sets, Odd Cycles, and 0-1/2 Chvatal-Gomory Cuts
contribution: With Caprara: separation of 0-1/2 Chvátal-Gomory cuts, NP-complete in general but polynomial in two special cases, by reductions and odd cut-set and odd cycle heuristics (one exact for a strong subclass), giving new separation algorithms for six polytopes.
problem_entry: A general subclass of Chvátal-Gomory cuts, defined by 0 and 1/2 multipliers (abstract).
key_idea: Separation through minimum-weight odd cut-sets and odd cycles in a suitable graph, exact for a subclass (abstract).
assumptions: Integer programs with CG derivations; six named polytopes as applications (abstract).
proof_devices: NP-completeness of 0-1/2 SEP and two polynomial special cases (abstract)
Reduction procedures for 0-1/2 SEP (abstract)
Odd cut-set and odd cycle heuristics, one exact for a subclass (abstract)
Dynamic program for a minimum-weight odd cycle in a digraph (appendix; abstract)
experiments: none mentioned in the abstract

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: Chvátal–Gomory derivation as validity proof and separation handle
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: One derivation-based cut family with one separation route (odd cut-sets, odd cycles) yields new separation algorithms for six polytopes; adds to the existing candidate (S069, S139, S028, S058, S057, S140).

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: Hardness in general, polynomial special cases alongside
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: 0-1/2 SEP is NP-complete in general but polynomial in two relevant special cases, and one heuristic is exact for a subclass; also S039, S048 and S035 in batch a2-01.

transferable: For a general cut family whose separation is NP-hard, find the subclass your heuristic separates exactly, and show that strong known families fall inside it (abstract).

quotes.text: We show that the associated separation problem, 0–1/2 SEP, is NP-complete in the general case, but polynomially solvable in two relevant special cases.
One of the two heuristics turns out to be exact for a subclass of 0–1/2 C–G cuts, which often contains wide families of strong inequalities.

title: A heuristic algorithm for the set covering problem

Systematic column fixing (abstract)
Modified step size and ascent direction in subgradient optimization (abstract)
Refining procedure (abstract)
experiments: Extensive computational results; no details in the abstract (abstract).
positioning: Improves the standard step-size and ascent-direction rules of subgradient optimization (abstract).

title: A polyhedral approach to the asymmetric traveling salesman problem
contribution: With Toth: a branch-and-cut for the ATSP with ATSP-specific facet-defining cuts, new separation algorithms and variable pricing for degenerate LPs, which clearly beats the best assignment-based codes on hard instances.
problem_entry: Instance classes on which assignment-relaxation branch-and-bound fails (abstract).
key_idea: Polyhedral branch-and-cut aimed at the hard instances, with new separation and pricing (abstract).
assumptions: ATSP instances, random and real-world, hard for AP-based codes (abstract).
proof_devices: Separation algorithms for some classes of facet-defining cuts (abstract)
Variable-pricing technique for highly degenerate primal LPs (abstract)
experiments: Several classes of random and real-world instances; on hard instances the branch-and-cut clearly outperforms the best AP-based algorithms (abstract).
positioning: Against the AP-based branch-and-bound algorithms from the literature (abstract).
writing: The rival's strong and weak classes are named before the aim; the outcome sentence opens with The outcome of the research (abstract).

The method is chosen to fit the instance class (step 2), but by strengthening the formulation with facet-defining cuts, the reflex Method 1 sets aside; 1997, before Method 1's dated evidence (2003-2017).

quotes.text: These algorithms perform very well for some instances (e.g., those with uniformly random integer costs), but very poorly for others.
